Article Title: Why’s CJI not on panel to pick CEC, Supreme Court asks government
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India

People must trust PM’s decisions, says SG Mehta amid challenge to authority

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Underscoring the need for an independent and impartial process for selection of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners, Supreme Court on Thursday said Election Commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. The court questioned why Parliament, while framing the law, decided not to include Chief Justice of India in the selection panel.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma said the CJI was part of selection panels for CBI director and Lokpal, and asked what could be the reason for excluding him from the process of selecting CEC and ECs — posts that are among the most important for a democracy. The court reserved its verdict on the Centre’s plea that the matter be referred to a constitution bench.The court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act, under which CEC and ECs are appointed by President on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of PM, leader of the opposition, and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by PM. SG Tushar Mehta argued that the court could not begin with an assumption that the PM would act against democratic principles.In 2023, a five-judge constitution bench of SC had directed that pending enactment of a law by Parliament, appointments should be made by a panel comprising the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition to infuse independence into the process. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a cabinet minister.Attorney general (AG) R Venkataramani and solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta urged the bench not to question the wisdom of Parliament, arguing that doing so would amount to interference with the independence of the legislature. The AG said Parliament’s legislative choice could not be questioned merely because another model was possible, and that “Parliament cannot be gagged”. The SG added that the three organs of the state — executive, legislature and judiciary — were independent, and their independence must be respected.“People must trust the Prime Minister. The office of the Prime Minister has a sanctity attached… If his decision is not to be trusted and is to be seen as necessarily a bad-faith exercise, then why not have a provision that even while selecting his cabinet he must consult some former judge or outsider?” SG Mehta said.Mehta added that one organ of the state could not proceed on the basis that the PM and other ministers would act in bad faith or against constitutional principles simply because they have the numerical majority.The bench clarified that there was no question of not trusting the PM. However, it asked the SG how many ministers in the government had cases pending against them, recalling that the court had earlier reposed trust in the elected government to ensure that people with criminal antecedents were not appointed as ministers.“It is not a lack of faith. The election commissioner has to be an independent person. Should there not be a show of fairness? We are not saying fairness has not been achieved by this committee. Just like justice is not only to be done, it has to be shown to be done, we are on the second part,” the bench said.Government requested that the petitions be referred to a larger constitution bench, arguing that an important question of law was involved. This plea was strongly opposed by senior advocates D Seshadri Naidu, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Prashant Bhushan and Sanjay Parikh, who contended that government was raising this ground after 20 days of hearing and should not be allowed to do so.In an affidavit, government countered the petitioners’ claim that the independence of Election Commission would be compromised by replacing CJI with a cabinet minister. It maintained that there was no flaw in the law passed by Parliament, and that free and fair elections had never been casualties even when appointments were made solely by the executive for over seven decades.Government described as hypothetical the suggestion that vesting the executive with exclusive authority in EC appointments would necessarily compromise the independence of the poll watchdog.
Article Summary: Supreme court says election commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. The court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 act, under which cec and ecs are appointed by president on the recommendation of a selection committee.

Article Title: 16 Indians, including 10 seamen, killed in Middle East conflict: Government
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Since the outbreak of the Middle East conflict earlier this year, sixteen Indian nationals, including 10 seafarers, have lost their lives in the region (eight in Oman, four in UAE, two in Kuwait and one each in Iran and Saudi Arabia) and 75 have been injured, said the government in Parliament.Responding to a written question in Rajya Sabha, MoS (MEA) Kirti Vardhan Singh said that in a separate accident not related to attacks, 12 Indian nationals lost their lives in Ras Laffan Gas Facility in Qatar."Government, in coordination with the host governments, has extended all possible assistance to the families of the deceased Indian nationals for early repatriation of the mortal remains to India.The injured Indian nationals received medical treatment in local hospitals.Indian Embassies and Consulates coordinated with the local authorities and the hospitals for regular updates on the health condition and extended all required assistance," said the minister.
Article Summary: 16 indian nationals, including 10 seafarers, have lost their lives in the region. 75 have been injured, said the government in parliament. Government has extended all possible assistance to the families of the deceased indian nationals for early repatriation of the mortal remains to india.

Article Title: After PM row, new Meta protocols for VIP accounts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: After the temporary removal of PM Narendra Modi's Facebook video a few days ago, Meta has introduced new protocols for handling the accounts of prominent individuals.Electronics and IT secretary S Krishnan told reporters on the sidelines of a CII event that Meta had informed govt that the additional safeguards were put in place after July 28. A meeting between Meta's global officials and govt is also scheduled within the next 7-10 days, Krishnan said on Thursday.Upcoming discussions between Meta and govt will cover both the policy and technical aspects of the incident, as well as Meta’s response to concerns raised by govt, electronics and IT secretary S Krishnan said Thursday. According to Krishnan, Meta has also written to govt expressing regret over the episode and outlining its understanding of the reasons behind removal of the video.“The company has expressed regret, and we will be meeting their global officials in the next 7-10 days,” Krishnan said, adding govt is continuing to examine Meta’s explanation.The development follows ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) summoning Meta’s senior global executives over the brief removal of PM’s Facebook post.Govt officials had earlier said they were not satisfied with the company’s explanation that the takedown was caused by an automated error and maintained the matter was ‘far from settled’. Krishnan said govt is examining representations submitted by messaging platforms regarding the proposed introduction of usernames, an issue on which MeitY had recently sought responses from companies.PM’s video was uploaded on July 23 during the CJP-led protests over alleged examination paper leaks. Meta later apologised over its removal on July 28, saying the content had been “removed in error” and that it was not the result of any govt directive or content policy action.
Article Summary: Meta has introduced new protocols for handling the accounts of prominent individuals. A meeting between meta's global officials and govt is also scheduled within the next 7-10 days. Pm’s video was uploaded on july 23 during the cjp-led protests over alleged examination paper leaks.

NEW DELHI: Amid the deepening Middle East crisis, PM Narendra Modi Thursday chaired what was the fourth special meeting of the cabinet committee on security (CCS) and directed establishment of a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers, serving on both domestic and foreign-flagged vessels, and their families."The PM said all efforts must be made to safeguard citizens as well as the Indian diaspora from the impact of this conflict," an official statement said. It added that Modi also addressed issues related to fertilisers, energy and safety of Indian diaspora and seafarers, while calling for a whole-of-government approach to tackle the challenges.The release said the meeting also assessed the fertiliser requirement for the ensuing rabi season and discussed alternative sources of fertilisers. "PM said that all measures be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilisers," it said.Persons familiar with the discussion said fertiliser stock was 30-35% higher than last year and there was no reason for any concern.Similarly, in the case of gas as well as crude oil, supplies were more than adequate, with cabinet secretary T V Somanathan in a presentation underlining that government’s strategy to diversify the sources had helped mitigate the risk.“Availability of adequate crude oil has enabled central public sector enterprise refineries to operate at utilisation levels exceeding 100%, ensuring continued production of petrol, diesel and other petroleum products. Initiatives have also been taken to expand PNG connections which have resulted in substantial increase in PNG connections,” it said.Besides, it said, government was also facilitating industrial substitution of LPG through expansion of the National Gas Grid, augmentation of LNG import and regasification infrastructure, expansion of city gas distribution networks, faster approvals for expansion of the pipeline infrastructure.PM stressed to ensure energy independence, emphasis should be made on renewable energy sources, including solar energy and other non-fossil-fuel based sources. The meeting took place amid escalation on multiple fronts in the Middle East region, including fresh US-Iran strikes and maritime and energy disruptions.“PM said a whole of government approach be continued to be adopted to tackle the challenges arising due to the crisis. He said that a unified coordinated mechanism be put in place for regular monitoring of all the developments to ensure expeditious implementation of appropriate measures to safeguard the interests of the citizens.”
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi chaired fourth special meeting of the cabinet committee on security. He directed establishment of a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers, serving on both domestic and foreign-flagged vessels.

Article Title: Calling registered AYUSH doctors 'quacks' has no legal basis: NCISM
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a move likely to intensify the debate over the status of traditional medicine practitioners, the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) has warned that calling duly registered AYUSH doctors "quacks" or "bogus doctors" has no legal basis and could violate their legal and constitutional rights.The commission said it had come to its notice that qualified practitioners holding recognised degrees in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa were being subjected to harassment, defamation and false characterisation through public notices, print and electronic media, social media platforms and other public forums.The NCISM said practitioners registered with the appropriate State Medical Councils for Indian Medicine and recognised under the Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970, and the NCISM Act, 2020, are legally recognised medical practitioners. It said the NCISM Act provides the statutory framework for regulating education, ethics and professional practice in Indian systems of medicine and confers legal rights and responsibilities on registered practitioners."There is no legal basis for describing such registered practitioners as 'quacks' or 'bogus doctors'," the commission said, adding that any individual, institution, media organisation or authority publicly using such terms may be acting contrary to the legal recognition granted under the NCISM Act, 2020, and may be infringing upon the practitioners' professional and constitutional rights.Reiterating its position, the commission said all duly qualified and registered practitioners of the Indian System of Medicine are legally recognised healthcare professionals and are entitled to the rights, protections and professional respect accorded to them under the law.The NCISM's stand is also consistent with the Centre's responses in Parliament, where the Ministry of AYUSH has repeatedly distinguished between unrecognised persons posing as AYUSH practitioners, who are liable for penal action under the law, and duly qualified and registered practitioners recognised under the NCISM Act.
Article Summary: The national commission for indian system of medicine (ncism) has warned that calling duly registered ayush doctors "quacks" or "bogus doctors" has no legal basis. The commission said qualified practitioners holding recognised degrees in ayurveda, unani, siddha and sowa-rigpa were being subjected to harassment, defamation and false characterisation.

Article Title: From LPG to Rabi fertilisers: PM Modi reviews Middle East crisis preparedness
Article Text:
PM Modi reviews Middle East crisis preparedness

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday chaired a high-level meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) to review the ongoing conflict in Middle East and assess India's preparedness to deal with its impact.The meeting reviewed the geopolitical situation, the availability of fuel and fertilisers, the safety of Indian citizens and the diaspora and measures to protect Indian seafarers operating in conflict zones. This was the fourth special CCS meeting held on the issue.During the meet, several top cabinet ministers including Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh and NSA chief Ajit Doval were also present.The Cabinet Secretary briefed the committee on the steps taken to ensure uninterrupted supplies of petroleum products, including crude oil, LPG and LNG. According to the briefing, India has diversified its LPG procurement sources and that the stock position of major petroleum products remains adequate.The government said sufficient crude oil supplies have enabled public sector refineries to operate at utilisation levels of over 100%, ensuring continued production of petrol, diesel and other fuels. It also highlighted ongoing efforts to expand piped natural gas (PNG) connections, strengthen the National Gas Grid, increase LNG import and regasification capacity and improve city gas distribution networks.The CCS also reviewed fertiliser availability ahead of the upcoming Rabi season. PM Modi further directed officials to take all necessary measures to ensure uninterrupted fertiliser supplies and explore alternate sources wherever required.The situation of Indian seafarers serving on domestic and foreign-flagged vessels in conflict zones also came up for discussion. PM directed the government to establish a dedicated mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families.Emphasising the need to protect Indian nationals overseas, PM Modi said every effort should be made to safeguard both Indian citizens and the Indian diaspora from the impact of the conflict, according to Press Information Bureau.PM Modi also stressed the importance of reducing dependence on conventional energy sources and called for greater emphasis on renewable energy, including solar power and other non-fossil fuel-based sources, to strengthen India's long-term energy security.Calling for a whole-of-government approach, PM Modi directed ministries and departments to continue working in close coordination. He also asked officials to establish a unified monitoring mechanism to regularly track developments in Middle East and ensure quick implementation of measures required to protect the interests of Indian citizens.The ongoing conflict in Middle East involving the United States, Iran and Israel has affected global energy markets and supply chains. India has also faced concerns over LPG supplies and energy security due to disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, leading the government to regularly review the evolving situation and preparedness measures.
Article Summary: Pm modi reviews middle east crisis preparedness at cabinet committee on security. Meeting reviewed geopolitical situation, availability of fuel and fertilisers. Measures to protect indian seafarers operating in conflict zones also discussed. This was the fourth special ccs meeting held on the issue.

Article Title: 'Criticise govt, don't denigrate India': Harish Salve on dissent and social media
Article Text:
Always remember, 'Sare Jahan Se Achcha Hindustan Humara', Harish Salve said.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Senior advocate Harish Salve on Wednesday said criticism aimed at "keep[ing] the government in control" is essential in a democracy, but urged people not to "denigrate India" in today's world of social media.Speaking about the turmoil in the Western world, particularly in Europe, the former solicitor general said that despite its internal challenges, the West remains united in resisting India's rise, which he said it still views as "a third-world country"."Trenchant criticisms within India of the government and its institutions is necessary to keep the government in control. But we should be very careful. Whatever we say, whatever we do in today's world of social media, do not denigrate India as a nation. Always remember, 'Sare Jahan Se Achcha Hindustan Humara'," Salve was quoted as saying by the news agency ANI.Speaking at the AK Sen Memorial Lecture and Photograph Unveiling Ceremony organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), Salve said holding those in power accountable is necessary in a constitutional democracy."One thing, as someone who resides outside India, is that India today is looked at with a great sense of respect.The Western world is in turmoil as we see every day. Europe feels orphaned. US is making people wonder whether it ever had a Constitution. But they unite when it comes to resisting India's ascent. They still find it hard to accept that a country of not white people, a country which they call a third-world country, is aspiring to be a leader of the world, has become the fourth largest economy in the world," Salve was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.The event marked the unveiling of a portrait of late Senior Advocate and former Union law minister AK Sen in Library No. 1 of the Supreme Court. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant joined Salve in unveiling the photograph.Several senior members of the legal fraternity attended the ceremony. SCBA President and Senior Advocate Vikas Singh paid tribute to Sen's contribution to the legal profession, while Attorney General for India R. Venkataramani also spoke about his legacy.Addressing the gathering, Chief Justice Surya Kant described Sen as a distinguished lawyer, scholar and statesman whose career reflected a lifelong commitment to justice and public service. He said the portrait would honour Sen's contribution while inspiring future generations of advocates."Today, we are not merely adorning our Library with a fitting tribute; we are enshrining in these walls the spirit of a life devoted to justice, intellect and public service... For every Advocate who passes through the Library, this portrait would be a silent reminder that our calling transcends personal ambition, that the practice of law and the stewardship of justice are sacred trusts in service of the Republic," the Chief Justice said.He added that the portrait should remind young lawyers of the values expected from members of the legal profession."A young lawyer rushing to Court with a first brief may pass this portrait. I hope the portrait will ask the more important questions that Mr Sen no doubt asked himself sometimes: Have I prepared enough? Have I been fair to the Court and to my opponent? Have I used the law to clarify, or merely to complicate?... May his presence here remind us that brilliance without balance is incomplete; that office without service is transient; and that law without humanity is barren," the Chief Justice said.
Article Summary: Senior advocate harish salve said criticism aimed at "keep[ing] the government in control" is essential in a democracy. He urged people not to "denigrate india" in today's world of social media. Salve spoke at the unveiling of a portrait of late senior advocate and former union law minister ak sen.

Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Wednesday likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj , saying that even Mughals had called the Maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat), just as the current generation is being called "cockroaches".Addressing a gathering during a book launch in Mumbai, Thackeray said those who had been dismissed as "cockroaches" belonged to Generation Z, roughly between the ages of 13 and 28 and drew a parallel how Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was only 17 when he captured Torna Fort, while Sant Dnyaneshwar was also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari."Those who were insulted as 'cockroaches' belong to what we now call Generation Z roughly from the ages of thirteen or fourteen to twenty-seven or twenty-eight. Wasn't Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj just about that age when he captured Torna Fort at seventeen? Even Shivaji Maharaj was called a 'Chuha' by Mughal. Wasn't Sant Dnyaneshwar also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari? Both faced tremendous opposition in their own time," Thackeray said.He said Shivaji Maharaj had challenged the Mughal Empire despite his young age, arguing that today's youth should not be belittled for speaking out.This comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted Gen Z terminology to sharpen their political messaging during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.From treasury bench members defending the Centre's reforms to opposition MPs criticising the government's handling of the NEET controversy, lawmakers turned to internet slang more commonly associated with social media than parliamentary debate.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj invoked Gen Z slang while backing the proposed legislation, using the phrase "clock it", a popular internet expression used to acknowledge or recognise something.Speaking in support of the Bill, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution."On the other hand, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra invoked Gen Z terminology while criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public outreach, arguing that young people were able to see through political messaging."If you want to win over the Gen Z, then making videos with different camera angles will not help. The prime minister needs to change the angle of his heart, not the angle of cameras," Priyanka said."Injustice has been done with youths under your government, accept the truth. Prime Minister Narendra Modi must take responsibility," she added.
Article Summary: Shiv sena (ubt) chief uddhav thackeray likened gen z to chhatrapati shivaji maharaj. He said that even mughals had called the maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat), just as the current generation is being called "cockroaches" this comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted gen z terminology.

Article Title: Spain migrant crisis: Military deployed as thousands cross border; 9 killed
Article Text:
Thousands crossed border into Spain

Spain has announced the deployment of its military to Ceuta after thousands of migrants crossed into the North African enclave from Morocco, triggering, what the authorities and people are describing as one of the territory's worst border crises in years. At least nine people died during the mass crossings.The government said the Armed Forces would assist the Civil Guard to “maintain security in the city of Ceuta.”, while Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska travelled to Ceuta on Friday to oversee the response.The latest crisis unfolded on Thursday when thousands of migrants crossed into Ceuta by swimming around breakwaters, using inflatable devices or scaling the border fence. Videos showing large crowds celebrating as they entered Spanish territory quickly spread on social media, highlighting the scale of the influx.Officials said the sudden surge overwhelmed security forces. "The situation is absolute chaos," said Rachid Sbihi, head of the association representing Civil Guard officers in Ceuta, adding that the border had "totally collapsed", as quoted by AP.Spanish authorities did not provide an official figure for the number of arrivals, but state broadcaster TVE estimated that between 2,000 and 3,000 migrants entered Ceuta within hours.Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas said the territory had already been receiving around 300 migrants by sea each day in recent weeks, leaving reception centres overstretched even before Thursday's influx.Read more: Videos of Moroccan migrants entering Spain after swimming around border barriers go viral Vivas urged Madrid to declare a national emergency and deploy the military, warning that the autonomous city lacked the capacity to manage the crisis on its own.Spain later confirmed that it had reached an agreement with Morocco to facilitate the return of migrants who entered Ceuta illegally, although no timeline for the repatriations has been announced. Spain's Interior Ministry said Moroccan authorities were cooperating to prevent further crossings and stop people attempting to reach the enclave.Morocco's embassy in Madrid blamed criminal networks involved in migrant smuggling and human trafficking for the mass crossings, saying Moroccan authorities did not support or encourage the movements.The reason behind the sudden influx remains unclear. Some local authorities suggested a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling, which bars the immediate return of migrants arriving by sea without due process, may have encouraged more people to attempt the crossing. However, migrant rights activists questioned that explanation, arguing that most migrants were unlikely to have been aware of the court's decision.The latest emergency echoes the 2021 Ceuta border crisis, when more than 8,000 migrants entered the enclave in just two days after Morocco was accused of relaxing border controls during a diplomatic dispute with Spain.Ceuta, along with Melilla, is one of the European Union's only two land borders with Africa and has long been a focal point for irregular migration into Europe.
Article Summary: Thousands of migrants crossed into ceuta from morocco on thursday. At least nine people died during the mass crossings. Spain has announced the deployment of its military to ceuta. The armed forces will assist the civil guard to ‘maintain security in the city’

Article Title: 10 climbers, including Nirmal Purja, missing after avalanche on Broad Peak in PoK's Gilgit-Baltistan
Article Text:
Who is Nirmal Purja?



Ten international climbers, including renowned Nepal-born mountaineer Nirmal Purja have gone missing after an avalanche struck Broad Peak, one of the world's highest mountains in Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan.According to the Alpine Club of Pakistan, the avalanche hit the expedition around midday on Thursday on the 8,047-metre (26,400-foot) Broad Peak in the Karakoram range, the Associated Press reported.The missing team comprises five Nepalese climbers, Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi from Hunza, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis, a Chinese climber identified only as Wang, and another foreign climber, the club said.The team has remained out of communication since the incident. However, a tracking device carried by Purja has continued to show movement, offering a glimmer of hope as rescuers race against time to reach the team.Speaking to Kantipur on Friday, Purja's business partner and Nepal lawmaker Mingma Gyabu Sherpa said data from the mountaineer's tracking device indicated that his location had changed after the avalanche."Initially, it appeared that he had been swept downhill by the avalanche," Sherpa was quoted as saying by The Kathmandu Post. "But after the point where the tracking had stopped, the location appears to have shifted again."Sherpa cautioned that the tracking data could not confirm Purja's condition but said it suggested some movement after the avalanche. He added that detailed information about the incident reached them only on Thursday evening, several hours after the avalanche struck.Poor weather has so far prevented helicopters from taking off, delaying aerial search-and-rescue operations. Sherpa said authorities were preparing to deploy helicopters on Friday morning if weather conditions improved.The club said it was working closely with government authorities to launch an immediate search-and-rescue operation. Its president, Maj Gen Irfan Arshad, and senior officials are coordinating efforts to mobilise helicopters and other rescue resources as soon as weather and operational conditions permit.Purja, also known as Nims Dai, is a Nepal-born British mountaineer and former Royal Marine. He joined the British Army in 2003 and became a Royal Marine in 2009.He rose to global prominence in 2019 after climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre peaks in just 189 days, setting a record at the time.His achievement was later featured in the Netflix documentary "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible." The record was surpassed in 2023 by a Norwegian climber and her Nepali Sherpa guide.Purja began his mountaineering career in 2012 after trekking to the Everest Base Camp. Instead of returning home as planned, he decided to climb Mount Everest , marking the start of his career as a high-altitude climber.
Article Summary: Ten international climbers missing after avalanche on broad peak. Avalanche hit the expedition around midday on thursday on the 8,047-metre (26,400-foot) broad peak in pakistan-occupied gilgit-baltistan. Tracking device carried by nirmal purja has continued to show movement.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes’ father reveals the ‘painful’ reason behind his latest court request amid probation
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes’ father reveals the ‘painful’ reason behind his latest court request amid probation (Image via Getty)

Why Patrick Mahomes Sr. wants his ankle monitor removed

Patrick Mahomes Sr.’s probation history and baseball career

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes Sr., the father of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, is asking a judge to let him remove the ankle monitor he has been wearing as part of his probation. According to court documents obtained by TMZ, his lawyer said the device has caused serious skin irritation, leaving his lower leg swollen and discolored. The filing also says Mahomes Sr. tried using a skin cream, but it did not improve the condition. His request comes after he completed extra testing ordered by his probation officer, including a voluntary hair-follicle test and a blood test, both of which he passed.The request is linked to the conditions of Patrick Mahomes Sr.’s probation. The former Major League Baseball pitcher was arrested for driving while intoxicated in February 2024. He later accepted a plea deal after admitting to his third DWI charge. Under that agreement, he received five years of probation, including one year of intensive supervision, and was required to wear an alcohol-monitoring ankle device.According to TMZ, Mahomes Sr.’s attorney told the court the monitor has caused ongoing medical problems. The filing says his lower leg became swollen and discolored, and even after applying a cream, the irritation did not go away. At one point, the monitor was moved to his other ankle, but the same problem happened there as well.The court filing also includes a doctor’s note supporting the request. Mahomes Sr.’s probation officer reportedly confirmed that he personally saw the swelling. Before considering the request, the officer asked Mahomes Sr. to take a voluntary hair-follicle test and a blood test. Court records say he passed both tests.Mahomes Sr.’s legal troubles did not end with his original plea agreement. He later violated the terms of his probation by drinking alcohol. As a result, the court extended his probation by two years. He was also ordered to complete a 16-week treatment program and serve 30 days in jail, with credit for time already served.Away from the courtroom, Mahomes Sr. is known for his long baseball career. The 55-year-old played 11 seasons in Major League Baseball, mostly as a relief pitcher, and finished with a 5.34 ERA. He is also the father of four children.His son, Patrick Mahomes II, followed a different path but shared the same love for baseball while growing up. Before becoming one of the NFL’s biggest stars, he was a standout baseball player in high school in Texas. He is now also a minority owner of the Kansas City Royals. Another family connection to baseball is former Minnesota Twins reliever LaTroy Hawkins, who played with Mahomes Sr. and is Patrick Mahomes II’s godfather.The court has not yet ruled on Mahomes Sr.’s request to remove the ankle monitor.
Article Summary: Patrick mahomes sr. is asking a judge to let him remove the ankle monitor he has been wearing as part of his probation. According to court documents, his lawyer said the device has caused serious skin irritation, leaving his lower leg swollen and discolored.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Saturday urged the Centre to accept the protesters' demands, alleging that the government was transporting tanks to Delhi while the student agitation continued."Ab aayega aur maza! The government must understand that it can either bomb the peaceful protesters using the tanks it is transporting to Delhi (I mean, what are they trying to do by transporting these? Kill their own children? Is this where we have come in Gandhi's India?) Or, accept demands. The time is ticking!" Das said in a post on X.He made the remarks while sharing a post by the Bharatiya Kisan Union announcing that it would join the ongoing student protest at Jantar Mantar.The development comes as CJP reiterated that it may adopt a "tough stance" if the Centre does not clarify its position on the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Speaking to reporters, CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka said the meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh was constructive, but added that the organisation was still awaiting the government's response to its primary demand."Yesterday's meeting yielded a positive response regarding compensation and legal matters, reaching an in-principle agreement. We hope to receive that written agreement today. However, no concrete decision has been made regarding our main demand. Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.""Mainstream media reports suggest sources are saying Pradhan will not step down. If he does not resign, the government should state it clearly, as there is no point in continuing these meetings. We will then decide on our next steps. If the government continues this approach, we will be forced to take a tough stance," Ranka said.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. Article Title: US restores $600 million for Gavi vaccine alliance, keeps WHO cut off
Article Text:
During his first term in 2020, Trump temporarily suspended US funding to the organisation.

The United States has approved the release of $600 million in funding for Gavi, the global vaccine alliance, but has decided that none of the money will be routed through the World Health Organization (WHO), dealing another financial setback to the UN health agency.In a joint statement, the US Department of State and the Department of Health and Human Services said the US government would not provide funding to the WHO through Gavi.The decision follows directions issued by President Donald Trump, who asked Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and secretary of state Marco Rubio to negotiate reforms with Gavi before any long-term US support is restored.Republican Senator Susan Collins, who had urged the administration to resume funding for the international immunisation programme, welcomed the move.According to the State Department, Gavi has agreed to work with its governing board and partner countries to gradually replace vaccines containing mercury with mercury-free alternatives. The latest decision continues Trump's long-running dispute with the WHO.During his first term in 2020, Trump temporarily suspended US funding to the organisation, accusing it of mishandling the Covid-19 pandemic and amplifying what he called China's "disinformation" about the virus.He argued that the WHO's actions contributed to the wider spread of the outbreak.At the time, the United States was the WHO's largest financial contributor, providing more than $400 million in 2019, which accounted for about 15 per cent of the organisation's budget.On the first day of his second term on January 20, 2025, Trump announced that the US would withdraw from the WHO and halted American financial contributions to the agency.Health experts have said the administration's decisions appear to be driven more by ideological considerations than by strategic public health priorities.The WHO receives funding through mandatory contributions from member states as well as voluntary donations from governments and other partners.With an annual budget of about $3.4 billion, the WHO operates on significantly fewer resources than the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, which received $9.3 billion in core funding in 2023.The organisation uses its funding to support vaccination campaigns and programmes to prevent and treat diseases such as polio, tuberculosis, HIV, malaria and measles, particularly in countries with limited healthcare systems.It also coordinates emergency health responses in conflict-affected regions, including Gaza, Sudan and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, among others.
Article Summary: The united states has approved the release of $600 million in funding for gavi, the global vaccine alliance. However, none of the money will be routed through the world health organization (who) the decision follows directions issued by president donald trump, who asked health and human services secretary robert f. kennedy jr. and secretary of state marco rubio to negotiate reforms.
